newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges serious negotiations in N. Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges serious negotiations in N. Ireland.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton urged Northern Ireland political leaders on Tuesday to engage in serious peace talks, and predicted they would be opened to the political wing of the IRA once it declared a cease-fire.

"I call on the political leaders to seize this precious opportunity and begin the hard but worthwhile work of negotiating a just and lasting settlement," Clinton said in a statement issued by the White House.
The multi-party talks resumed in Belfast Tuesday after a three-month hiatus.
Sinn Fein, the Irish Republican Army's political wing, has not been allowed to participate until the outlawed guerrilla group reinstates a cease-fire.
"If the IRA declares and implements an unequivocal cease-fire, I am confident that Sinn Fein will be invited to add its voice to the other parties at the table," Clinton said.
